articles.title: The Brisbane 2032 Olympics logo is hiding a triple design in plain sight
articles.summary: The Brisbane 2032 Olympic emblem combines three ideas in a single vivid form: an Olympic flame, the crest of Australia's native cockatoo, and the shape of Queensland. Its pink-and-red form gives the identity an energetic, playful character intended to feel distinctly connected to the host region. The identity was accidentally revealed early through an explainer uploaded to Brisbane 2032's YouTube channel.

articles.title: John Ternus is taking a more ‘hands-on' role in Apple's design teams as CEO
articles.summary: Apple CEO John Ternus has reportedly become deeply involved with the company's industrial design and human interface teams, working in the design studio several times a week and sometimes visiting multiple times per day. Rather than appointing a new chief design officer, Apple has Molly Anderson leading industrial design and Steve Lemay leading human interface design, with Ternus acting as the overarching decision-maker. Apple is also rebuilding teams depleted by departures to companies including Meta and OpenAI through internal promotions and external hires.

articles.title: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results
articles.summary: OpenAI is adding visual display ads alongside images generated in ChatGPT, starting later this month in the US with a small group of advertisers. The ads will be clearly labeled and, according to OpenAI, will not influence ChatGPT's answers. The company is also expanding ad measurement partnerships and developing brand suitability evaluations as it builds an ad-supported business for users on free and low-cost plans.

articles.title: Training AI to Paint with Code
articles.summary: A language model was trained with reinforcement learning to create watercolor images by writing editable p5.brush JavaScript rather than generating fixed image files, giving people direct control over the resulting artifact. Early training exposed problems with overly complex reward systems, while switching from absolute scores to pairwise comparisons against a hand-rated reference pool produced better images with dramatically shorter code. The experiment shows that applying reinforcement learning to creative work is fundamentally a design problem: subjective qualities like taste need carefully constructed reward structures that provide direction without forcing the model toward a single aesthetic.

articles.title: 10 Uncomfortable UX Lessons from Real Design Mistakes
articles.summary: Ten uncomfortable lessons from real design mistakes offer a way to make better design choices before running more UX tests. Minimalism failed on an ERP shipment form, and a standard landing page beat an artistic, scroll-snapping one in an A/B test. Other lessons favor preventing errors over recovering from them, and giving users an opt-out instead of forcing AI into manual workflows.

articles.title: What Are the Principles of Prototyping?
articles.summary: A prototype is a way to learn something before making a bigger commitment, in any form, from an email or text message to an event. Nine principles, refined by 124 people at Services Week 2026, hold that a prototype answers a question, is tested with future users, and can be archived. The tools have changed, with AI-assisted ones now in the mix, but the purpose and principles of prototyping have not.

articles.title: Inspect Any Page with No Site Access Requested (Website)
articles.summary: A free, open-source browser extension that inspects layout, styles, color, type, and assets on any page.

articles.title: Turning Product Managers and Product Designers into Product Builders (Website)
articles.summary: AutonomyAI lets PMs and designers create production code changes for engineering approval, so engineers stay focused on what only they can build.

articles.title: RuneIcons - Beautiful Icons for Your Next Project (Website)
articles.summary: Rune Icons is a free, open-source library of more than 900 hand-drawn icons available in outline, duotone, fill, pixel, and glass styles, with browser-based controls for editing paths, stroke, size, color, and motion before copying them as SVG or JSX.

articles.title: Workflow Lab: From Design System to Campaign in Figma Weave
articles.summary: A product designer at a fictional museum uses Figma Weave to turn the museum's design system into campaign collateral for a new exhibition. Image Describer nodes read existing designs and color families, and the Gen Effect node gives every image a shared look through color grading and hazy edges. The Figma node stays connected, so design-system updates flow downstream, and the node graph can be reused for future shows or published as a Weave tool.

articles.title: Design is a Nice-to-Have
articles.summary: Design feels like a nice-to-have again, according to a designer who now builds software himself and finds news about design craft and tools flat. Once programming became trivial, design lost the spotlight it briefly held when SaaS commoditized software and distribution was the hardest part. Craft still matters, but a "good enough" UX suffices, since usefulness to the market was always what mattered most.

articles.title: Brand Identity: Koto's Stack Overflow Rebrand
articles.summary: Koto has repositioned Stack Overflow as a source of human-validated knowledge in an AI-first world, consolidating its portfolio and building the identity around the concept “Always in Build.” A simplified stack-shaped logo expands into a generative visual language of geometry that continuously reformats and rebuilds, supported by an expanded orange-led palette and the custom Stack Sans typeface with distinctive notched letterforms. A custom generative tool lets Stack Overflow's team produce new compositions at scale, while the system stays restrained inside the product and becomes more expressive across campaigns and the Developer Survey.

articles.title: Seven Reasons Non-Artists Need a Drawing Pad on Their Desk
articles.summary: Non-artists can put the handmade Japanese Drawing Pad to seven uses, from brain-dumping to-do lists and mind-mapping to journaling and doodling away stress.

articles.title: Télio Péron Blends Photoreal Detail with Supernatural Imagination to Create 3D Environments That Never Fully Explain Themselves
articles.summary: French 3D artist Télio Péron grounds slightly impossible elements, from glowing artifacts to folklore creatures, in photoreal forests, moss, and weathered wood.
